_note_scope: Run-level provenance and generation metadata. This file answers WHEN / HOW / BY WHAT a capture was produced - as opposed to the config files, which declare WHAT to produce. Nothing here is an input to the sim; it is all stamped at or after generation time. Feeds directly into the data card (Phase 1 step 10.iv).

_file_map.CARLA_config.json: HOW the sim runs - server, world settings, conventions, presets
_file_map.ego_config.json: WHAT the ego is - blueprint + sensor rig (static across all scenes)
_file_map.scene_description.json: WHAT to capture - the 12-scene matrix + split policy
_file_map.metadata.json: THIS FILE - run provenance, results, cost

_note_runs: A run = one execution of the capture pipeline over a set of scenes, stamped independently. Every run is SPLIT-PURE and MAP-PURE: split-pure because the offline processor selects work by run-level split (process.py --split train processes exactly the runs flagged train), and map-pure because CARLA's client threads crash on a world reload after a prior scene's sensors ran (PyEval_SaveThread: NULL tstate), so each map gets its own client process. Runs 1-5 are the initial 12-scene matrix; top-up rounds append as run 6 onward with the split they are topping up.

runs._note_partition: Town04 / train. The split flag is what process.py matches on; every scene listed here must carry split='train' in scene_description.json or the processor refuses to run.

config_hashes._note: SHA256 of each config file as it existed at generation time. This is what lets you prove which exact config produced which data - if a config changes later, the hash mismatch tells you the dataset is stale. Cheap to compute, and a strong reproducibility signal. Identical across runs 1-3 (same configs); the point is the config-to-data binding, not per-run variation.

provenance._note_carla_version: The version that ACTUALLY ran. CARLA_config.json pins the intended version; this records what the server reported. A mismatch is a bug worth catching.

compute._note_cost: Track this per run; sum runs 1-3 for the matrix total. 'Generated a 7k-frame labeled AV dataset for $X of spot GPU' is a concrete number worth quoting (Project Outline section 7).

results._note_interruptions: Spot instances can be reclaimed mid-run. Captures stream to S3 per scene (step 7.iii), so an interruption should cost at most the current scene - record it here if it happens so gaps are explainable later.

class_histogram._status: FILL AFTER OFFLINE PROCESSING (step 9.v), PER RUN. The DATASET decision (top-up? / fine vs coarse) is made on the SUM across runs 1-3, since a class can be starved in one map but healthy overall.
class_histogram._note_preset: Counts below are for class_map preset 'fine' (7 classes). Per the Phase 1 doc each class wants 500-1500 instances. Cars will be abundant; motorcycle and the three sign classes are the at-risk ones.
class_histogram._note_per_split: Record per split, not just totals - a class that is healthy overall but absent from test tells you nothing on test.
class_histogram._note_decision: If motorcycle is starved -> flip class_map.active_preset to 'coarse' (free, no re-capture). If sign classes are starved -> that needs actual top-up scenes on sign-dense routes, since no re-mapping conjures sign instances that were never captured.
